s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea with signs of heart failure and preserved ejection fraction
salient_findings: Systolic murmur at the aortic and mitral areas
Pulmonary congestion and pleural effusion on chest radiography
key_facts: 53-year-old man
History of congenital ventricular septal defect repaired in childhood
Aortic valve and septal patch replacements
Permanent atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation
Chronic hepatitis C–related liver disease
Prior admission for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Jugular venous distension
Irregular rhythm
2/6 systolic murmur at the aortic and mitral areas
Decreased breath sounds at the right lung base
Peripheral edema
Atrial fibrillation with left bundle branch block on ECG
Pulmonary congestion and right basal pleural effusion on chest radiography
Dilated left ventricle with preserved ejection fraction on echocardiography
Severe prosthesis–patient mismatch
Moderate mitral regurgitation
Severe tricuspid regurgitation
Estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure of 50 mmHg

shortlist.label: Prosthesis-patient mismatch
shortlist.why_kept: Severe prosthesis–patient mismatch suggested by elevated transprosthetic gradients and low effective orifice area index

shortlist.label: Tricuspid regurgitation
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation noted on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Mitral regurgitation
shortlist.why_kept: Moderate mitral regurgitation observed on echocardiography

shortlist.why_kept: Estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure of 50 mmHg

shortlist.label: Diastolic dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and signs of diastolic dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of aortic valve replacement and echocardiography revealed a normally functioning mechanical aortic prosthesis but with elevated transprosthetic gradients and a low effective orifice area index, indicating severe prosthesis-patient mismatch, which can lead to heart failure symptoms and signs as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Tricuspid regurgitation
rejected.why: Although present, it is not the primary cause of the patient's symptoms and signs, which are more consistent with left-sided heart disease and prosthesis-patient mismatch.

rejected.label: Mitral regurgitation
rejected.why: Moderate mitral regurgitation is present, but it is not the primary cause of the patient's symptoms, which are more consistent with prosthesis-patient mismatch and its consequences.

rejected.label: Pulmonary hypertension
rejected.why: Estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure is elevated, but it is not the primary diagnosis, as the patient's symptoms and signs are more consistent with prosthesis-patient mismatch and left-sided heart disease.

rejected.label: Diastolic dysfunction
rejected.why: The patient has a preserved ejection fraction, which suggests that diastolic dysfunction is not the primary cause of the patient's symptoms and signs, which are more consistent with prosthesis-patient mismatch and its consequences.
